# Lending rules before the score (generated by `make policy`)

Each rule sits at the edge of the loans Lending Club approved in 2007-2014, where the scorecard's evidence ends. Debt-to-income including the new loan uses each loan's real instalment here; for a new application it is computed at 12.64% (the average 2007-2014 rate) or the break-even rate, if higher.

| rule (decline if)                                       |   approved loans breaking it |   share |   their default rate |
|:--------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------:|--------:|---------------------:|
| FICO score below 660                                    |                          489 | 0.00145 |                0.309 |
| annual income below $10,000                             |                          287 | 0.00085 |                0.157 |
| loan above $35,000                                      |                            0 | 0       |              nan     |
| loan above 50 % of annual income                        |                          260 | 0.00077 |                0.227 |
| debt-to-income above 40 % before this loan              |                            0 | 0       |              nan     |
| debt-to-income above 50 % including this loan's payment |                         1576 | 0.00466 |                0.261 |
| more than 7 credit inquiries in 6 months                |                          248 | 0.00073 |                0.363 |
| revolving balances above the credit limit (over 100 %)  |                          833 | 0.00246 |                0.196 |

Together the rules would have declined 3,585 of 337,996 approved loans (1.06%). Their default rate: 24.7%, against 13.0% for the rest.
